Tess: Heads-up — I'm sketching a tiny RFC to align status -> routing buckets + console badging + telemetry labels. Noticed mismatch between routing layer's 'degraded' and client-facing phrasing. Thoughts?
Aaron: Yep. Saw a customer where API returned 503 but our routing marked it 'degraded' and SDK showed a retry hint. Confusing for integrators.
Priya: Console also shows a 'fallback' badge on routes that are actually queued shards. UX leads to mistaken expectations.
Marta: Maybe we define 3 canonical consumer-facing buckets: `terminal`, `transient_retriable`, `soft_fallback` — each with explicit routing semantics + telemetry tag + HTTP mapping.
Tess: Draft mapping (very rough):
```
HTTP 400-499 -> terminal (client error, no retry)
HTTP 429 -> transient_retriable (rate-limit; include quota header + retry-after)
HTTP 500 -> transient_retriable (short-lived server error; can auto-retry)
HTTP 503 -> soft_fallback (fallback to cheaper model/region; surface console badge)
Routing-layer fallback event -> soft_fallback (emit `rw.routing.fallback` telemetry)
```
Aaron: Couple Qs — do we expose a header that tells SDKs what happened? SDKs currently look for `x-rw-retry` and `retry-after`.
Priya: We should avoid overloading `retry-after`. Propose `x-rw-hint: terminal|retryable|fallback` and `x-rw-reason: quota|capacity|model_fallback` (structured but short).
Marta: +1. Also add `rw.telemetry.status_bucket` tag for backend traces and ES logs so dashboards can roll up counts.
Tess: On console UX: replace ambiguous 'fallback' badge with 'soft-fallback' + short tooltip explaining 'requests routed to variant with different latency/cost' and link to rollout page.
Aaron: Rollout plan: implement header + telemetry, do 5% canary routing (dedicated canary pool) for 48h, then flip for 50% then 100% if no regressions.
Priya: Need sampling guidance — telemetry should sample full traces for `terminal` and `soft_fallback` but only 1% for successful requests to reduce cost.
Marta: Also adjust alerts: treat burst of `soft_fallback` as capacity pressure signal, not immediate incident unless >10% for 30m.
eng-bot: deploy queued: infra/telemetry-pipeline v2 -> canary env
Tess: I'll write a short RFC with the mapping + header names + console copy. Assigning follow-ups: @Aaron to update SDK parsing, @Priya to update console copy, @Marta to hook telemetry labels.
Aaron: Ack. I'll add SDK tests for header parsing and fallback behavior.
Priya: I'll draft the console tooltip and a small FAQ blurb.
Marta: Will add telemetry knobs and dashboard queries. We'll also include a small eval to check model-quality on fallback variants.
Tess: Thanks all — aim to land RFC by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
